The MassINC Polling Group & CommonWealth Beacon
Massachusetts Ballot Questions Poll
Survey of 800 Massachusetts likely voters
Field Dates: September 14 - 22, 2026
Thinking about the November election, how do you plan to vote?
Vote by mail 31%
Vote in person 65%
Unsure 3%
As you may have heard, the Trump administration wants the Postal Service to reject mail-in ballots that do
not match a voter database. Does this news make you less likely to vote by mail, more likely, or does it not
make a difference?

More likely to vote by mail 17%
Makes no difference 56%

ASK ALL
There will be 9 questions that appear on your ballot in November. We will now ask you about each.
Question 1 concerns records held by the State Legislature and the Governor’s office. A “yes” vote would make
most records held by the Legislature and the Office of the Governor public records under the Massachusetts
Public Records Law. A “no” vote would ma ke no change to the Massachusetts Public Records law. If the
election for this measure were held today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 63%
No 14%
Undecided 23%
Prefer not to say <1%
Question 2 concerns collective bargaining for the Committee for Public Counsel Services, which provides
public defenders to defendants who cannot afford them. A “yes” vote would specify that Committee for Public
Counsel Services employees may form a union to collectively bargain with their employer. A “no” vote would
make no change to the law governing labor relations for Committee for Public Counsel Service employees. If
the election for this measure were held today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 48%
No 25%
Undecided 26%
Prefer not to say 1%
The MassINC Polling Group 3

Question 3 concerns primary elections for political offices. A “yes” vote would eliminate separate party
primaries for state elections and require a single primary in which all candidates appear on one ballot, voters
could vote for any candidate, and the top two candidates would advance to the general elect ion. A “no” vote
would make no change to the laws governing primary elections. If the election for this measure were held
today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 43%
No 36%
Undecided 20%
Prefer not to say 1%
Question 4 concerns registering to vote. A “yes” vote would permit eligible citizens to register to vote or to
update their voter registration address at their polling place on Election Day. A “no” vote would make no
change to the laws governing voter registration. If the election for this measure were held today, would you
vote yes or no?
Yes 53%
No 33%
Undecided 14%
Prefer not to say 1%
Question 5 concerns the limit on how much revenue the state can collect in a given year. A “yes” vote would
change the limit on state revenue collection, tying it to prior year collections plus average wage and salary
growth, and provide for a rebate of re venue exceeding that limit. A “no” vote would make no change in the law
relative to state revenue collection. If the election for this measure were held today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 47%
No 26%
Undecided 25%
Prefer not to say 1%
Question 6 concerns creating a fund for nature conservation, subject to appropriation by the legislature. A
“yes” vote would create a fund that could be utilized for natural resource conservation that would receive
some state taxes collected on the sale and use of sporting goods and recreational vehicles, and the use of golf
courses. A “no” vote would not create this natural resource conservation fund or change how sales an d use
taxes are spent. If the election for this measure were held today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 56%
No 24%
Undecided 20%
Prefer not to say <1%
Question 7 concerns relaxing zoning rules for single- family homes. A “yes” vote would allow single -family
homes to be built on lots of 5,000 square feet or more in residential areas, subject to reasonable local
regulation of certain aspects of those homes. A “no” vote would make no change to the law relative to
building single-family homes. If the election for this measure were held today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 51%
No 24%
Undecided 24%
Prefer not to say 1%
The MassINC Polling Group 4

Question 8 concerns recreational marijuana. A “yes” vote would prohibit the legalization, regulation, and
taxation of the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana, and change the penalties for possession of
marijuana. A “no” vote would make no chang e to the law relative to marijuana. If the election for this
measure were held today, would you vote yes or no?
Yes 27%
No 61%
Undecided 11%
Prefer not to say 1%
Question 9 asks voters to approve or repeal an existing law regarding firearms. A “yes” vote would keep in
place the law, which increases the regulation of firearms, including ghost guns, machine guns, and assault-
style weapons. A “no” vote would repeal th e law. If the election for this measure were held today, would you
vote yes or no?
Yes 70%
No 18%
Undecided 11%
Prefer not to say 1%
Just to clarify, do you think the firearm law as described above should be kept in place, or should it be
repealed?
Kept in place 65%
Repealed 19%
Undecided 15%
Prefer not to say 1%
In 2024, voters passed a ballot question that gave the State Auditor the right to audit the State Legislature. Do
you support or oppose that decision to let the Auditor audit the Legislature?
Support 72%
Oppose 7%
Unsure 21%

About the poll
These results are based on a survey of 800 likely voters in the November 2026 election in Massachusetts.
Responses were collected via online survey interviewing September 14 - 22, 2026. Results were weighted by
race, age, gender, education, political party, and county to reflect known and estimated population
parameters for Massachusetts likely voters. The credibility interval for this survey is +/- 4 percentage points at
the 95% confidence level, inclusive of the design effect. This project was conducted by The MassINC Polling
Group and sponsored by CommonWealth Beacon .
